completed_unit.target: Cargo cargo vendor documented output and offline behavior
completed_unit.finding: Official Cargo documentation states that cargo vendor copies crates.io and git dependencies into a specified local directory and, after completion, prints the configuration needed to use those vendored sources to stdout for addition or redirection into .cargo/config.toml. The same command exposes --offline, which prevents network access but can only proceed from locally available data and may change dependency resolution, and --frozen, which combines --locked and --offline.
completed_unit.phase1_interpretation: This verifies that Cargo provides a repository-local dependency materialization/configuration mechanism and a documented no-network execution mode. It does not establish a scheduled-Chat-native Cargo executor or eliminate the need to run cargo vendor somewhere. Therefore the Chat-parity hard gate remains open: vendor generation is still an unresolved execution dependency under the tested scope.

scope_guard: Evidence is limited to documented cargo vendor behavior, its printed source configuration, and --offline/--frozen semantics. It does not prove dependencies are already cached, cargo vendor can execute inside scheduled Chat, a build is end-to-end offline, or richer-mode outcome parity.
residual_uncertainty: A Chat-exposed Cargo executor remains unestablished.
No cargo vendor command was executed, so actual vendor directory contents and emitted configuration were not observed.
The documentation says offline mode relies on locally available crates/index data and can resolve differently; the prerequisite acquisition path remains unverified in this leaf.
End-to-end richer-mode outcome parity remains unverified.
